Business situation: Budgeting total revenue or total units
In this simulation: Mean order $97.63, pulled up by 6 corporate orders
Watch out for: A few outliers can steer the whole model

Business situation: Describing a typical customer or week
Kind of error that hurts most: Every dollar of miss counts the same
In this simulation: Median order $60.85, barely moved by them
Watch out for: Totals built from medians come up short

Business situation: Noisy data with an occasional giant
Kind of error that hurts most: Small misses matter, giants shouldn't steer
In this simulation: $2.10 per ad dollar vs. $2.59 with squared error
Watch out for: The switch point (delta) is a judgment call

Loss that fits: Pinball loss at a high quantile, set by the cost ratio
In this simulation: q = 0.75 saves $859 a year vs. the squared-error model
Watch out for: The cost ratio has to be estimated honestly

Loss that fits: Pinball loss at a low quantile
In this simulation: Waste at 2x the cost of a miss: best quantile about 0.35

Business situation: Planning for a range, not a single number
Loss that fits: A pair of pinball losses, such as 10% and 90%
In this simulation: A 10% to 90% range about 69 boxes wide held 83% of test weeks
Watch out for: Ranges that are too narrow to be useful

Business situation: Deciding who gets an ad, an offer, or a call
Kind of error that hurts most: Paying for people who won't buy vs. missing people who would
Loss that fits: Log loss (cross-entropy), then a cutoff set by the costs
In this simulation: 11% cutoff earns $4,664 per 10,000 visitors vs. $650 at 50%

Business situation: Sorting leads into yes or no
Kind of error that hurts most: Confident wrong answers on rare, valuable cases
Loss that fits: Hinge loss only if a yes-or-no is all you need
In this simulation: Default hinge model retargets no one; cost-weighted version stops working at $6 ads
Watch out for: No probabilities, so no expected value
